subject: AI & Agents
title: Reasoning Models: Thinking Step by Step
description: Learn Reasoning Models: Thinking Step by Step in one minute.

hook.text: Instead of answering instantly, what if AI paused, planned, and reasoned through complex problems?

buildup.text: Chain-of-thought prompting showed that making models explain their reasoning improves accuracy.

discovery.text: Models like o1 are trained to generate internal reasoning chains before producing a final answer.

twist.text: Slower responses can be better. Thinking takes time — even for machines.

climax.text: Reasoning models solve math and logic problems that standard LLMs consistently fail at.

punchline.text: The smartest answer isn't always the fastest one.

quiz.question: How do reasoning models improve over standard language models?
options: They generate step-by-step reasoning before answering
They skip reasoning to answer faster
They only work on simple questions

details.summary: Reasoning models like OpenAI's o1 generate extended chains of thought before answering, spending more compute time to produce more accurate responses on complex problems like math, logic, and coding.
details.whyItMatters: Reasoning models represent a shift from fast pattern matching to deliberate thinking. They show that AI can trade speed for accuracy, opening the door to more reliable complex problem-solving.
takeaways: Reasoning models spend extra compute thinking before answering
Chain-of-thought processing improves accuracy on complex tasks
They trade speed for more reliable answers on hard problems

faq.question: How are reasoning models different from regular LLMs?
faq.answer: Regular LLMs generate answers token by token in one pass. Reasoning models generate extended internal reasoning chains first, allowing them to work through complex problems step by step before producing a final answer.

faq.question: What tasks benefit most from reasoning models?
faq.answer: Math, logic puzzles, coding, scientific analysis, and any task requiring multi-step deduction. For simple questions, standard models are faster and equally accurate, making reasoning models best reserved for hard problems.
